reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 7.1.1 leaves each Party owning its own inventions and pre-existing IP with no assignment of AbbVie (our) IP to Harpoon; Section 7.1.4(a) channels personnel/subcontractor results to the commissioning Party; Section 3.8.2(c) makes all Regulatory Documentation, Approvals and Labeling AbbVie's sole property with confirmatory assignment obligations on Harpoon; Section 5.6.2 negates any implied licence of AbbVie IP.

Joint ownership under Section 7.1.2 does not trip the walk-away trigger because each Party expressly has the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without consent or accounting, i.e. an unrestricted exploitation right; Harpoon retaining its platform technology is expressly accepted by the rule.

Deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') passes, consistent with the compliant classification; the rationale's failure to expressly discuss the joint-ownership carve-out and the redacted provisos in 7.1.2 is a minor gap that does not change the outcome.
